problems.name: Unique Paths
problems.question: Given an m x n grid, a robot starts at the top-left and can move only right or down. Return the number of paths to the bottom-right.
problems.constraints: 1 <= m, n <= 100; answer is at most 2 * 10^9.

examples.explanation: The paths are DDR, DRD, and RDD in move notation.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(n). 1D row DP updates path counts left to right.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Memoized recursion computes each cell once.

problems.name: Unique Paths II
problems.question: Given an m x n grid where 1 marks an obstacle and 0 marks open space, return the number of right/down paths from top-left to bottom-right.
problems.constraints: 1 <= m, n <= 100; obstacleGrid[i][j] is 0 or 1.

examples.explanation: Two paths go around the obstacle.
Only the down-right path is open.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(n). A 1D row DP resets blocked cells to zero.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Memoized recursion stores path counts per cell.

problems.name: Minimum Path Sum
problems.question: Given a grid of non-negative numbers, return the minimum sum path from top-left to bottom-right moving only right or down.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(n). Rolling row DP keeps minimum cost for each column.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Memoized recursion stores minimum suffix cost per cell.

problems.name: Triangle
problems.question: Given a triangle array, return the minimum path sum from top to bottom by moving to adjacent numbers on the next row.
problems.constraints: 1 <= triangle.length <= 200; triangle[i].length == i + 1; -10000 <= values <= 10000.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(rows^2); Space O(rows). Bottom-up DP keeps one row of costs.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(rows^2); Space O(rows^2). Memoized recursion stores each triangle position.

problems.name: Longest Common Subsequence
problems.question: Given two strings, return the length of their longest common subsequence.
problems.constraints: 1 <= text1.length, text2.length <= 1000; strings contain lowercase English letters.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(n). Rolling row DP stores LCS lengths for the second string.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Memoized recursion computes each pair of indexes once.

problems.name: Edit Distance
problems.question: Given two words, return the minimum number of insert, delete, and replace operations needed to convert word1 into word2.
problems.constraints: 0 <= word1.length, word2.length <= 500; words contain lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Five edits are required in an optimal sequence.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(n). Rolling DP keeps previous row and current row values.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Memoized recursion solves each index pair once.

problems.name: Regular Expression Matching
problems.question: Given string s and pattern p containing . and *, return whether p matches the entire string. Dot matches any single character and star repeats the previous element zero or more times.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 20; 1 <= p.length <= 20; pattern is valid and uses lowercase letters, dot, and star.

examples.explanation: The pattern covers only one a.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Bottom-up DP fills string-pattern states.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Memoized recursion stores each pair of indexes.

problems.name: Wildcard Matching
problems.question: Given string s and pattern p containing ? and *, return whether p matches the entire string. ? matches one character and * matches any sequence including empty.
problems.constraints: 0 <= s.length, p.length <= 2000; p contains lowercase letters, ? and *.

examples.explanation: The pattern does not cover the full string.
? matches c but a does not match b.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(n). Rolling pattern DP can match every string-pattern state.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Memoized recursion stores each pair of indexes.

problems.name: Distinct Subsequences
problems.question: Given strings s and t, return the number of distinct subsequences of s equal to t.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length, t.length <= 1000; strings contain English letters.

examples.explanation: There are three ways to delete one b.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(n). 1D DP updates target positions backward.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Memoized recursion stores source and target indexes.

problems.name: Interleaving String
problems.question: Given s1, s2, and s3, return true if s3 is formed by interleaving s1 and s2 while preserving the order of characters from each string.
problems.constraints: 0 <= s1.length, s2.length <= 100; 0 <= s3.length <= 200; strings contain lowercase letters.

examples.explanation: s3 can be formed while preserving both orders.
No valid interleaving matches all characters.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(n). Rolling DP tracks feasible counts from s2 for each s1 prefix.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Memoized recursion solves each pair of consumed lengths once.

problems.name: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
problems.question: Given a string s, return the length of the longest subsequence that reads the same forward and backward.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 1000; s contains lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: bb is the longest palindromic subsequence.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n). Rolling interval DP stores results for the current left boundary.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n^2). Memoization stores every interval once.

problems.name: Longest Palindromic Substring
problems.question: Given a string s, return the longest contiguous substring that is a palindrome.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 1000; s contains digits and English letters.

examples.explanation: aba is also a valid longest answer.
bb is the longest palindromic substring.
A single character is a palindrome.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n^2). Boolean interval DP marks palindromic substrings.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n^2). Memoized palindrome checks are reused while scanning intervals.

problems.name: Palindromic Substrings
problems.question: Given a string s, return the number of contiguous substrings that are palindromes.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 1000; s contains lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Only a, b, and c are palindromes.
All three singles, two aa substrings, and aaa count.
The full string and inner palindromes are included.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n^2). Interval DP computes palindrome status once per substring.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n^2). Recursive palindrome checks are memoized for all intervals.

problems.name: Coin Change II
problems.question: Given coin denominations and an amount, return the number of combinations that make the amount. Each coin can be used unlimited times.
problems.constraints: 1 <= coins.length <= 300; 1 <= coins[i] <= 5000; 0 <= amount <= 5000.

examples.explanation: The empty combination makes amount zero.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * amount); Space O(amount). 1D unbounded knapsack adds current coin contributions left to right.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n * amount); Space O(n * amount). Memoization stores coin index and remaining amount.

problems.name: Target Sum
problems.question: Given nums and target, assign either plus or minus before every number. Return how many assignments evaluate to target.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 20; 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; -1000 <= target <= 1000; total sum <= 1000.

examples.explanation: Each zero can be plus or minus without changing the sum.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * sum); Space O(sum). Offset DP stores counts for reachable signed sums.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n * sum); Space O(n * sum). Memoization stores index and offset running sum.

problems.name: Ones and Zeroes
problems.question: Given binary strings strs and limits m zeros and n ones, return the maximum number of strings that can be chosen without exceeding either limit.
problems.constraints: 1 <= strs.length <= 600; 1 <= strs[i].length <= 100; 0 <= m, n <= 100.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(k * m * n * L); Space O(m * n). Descending capacity loops implement 0/1 knapsack.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(k * m * n * L); Space O(k * m * n). Memoization stores index and two capacities.

problems.name: Last Stone Weight II
problems.question: Given stone weights, repeatedly smashing stones is equivalent to splitting stones into two groups. Return the minimum possible remaining weight.
problems.constraints: 1 <= stones.length <= 30; 1 <= stones[i] <= 100.

examples.explanation: Groups can be split with sums 11 and 12.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * total); Space O(total). 0/1 subset DP finds the closest half-sum.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n * total); Space O(n * total). Memoization stores index and current bounded subset sum.

problems.name: Partition Equal Subset Sum
problems.question: Given nums, return true if the array can be split into two subsets with equal sum.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 200; 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

examples.explanation: No subset reaches half of 11 because the total is odd.
The target is 6, but no subset sums to 6.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * target); Space O(target). Descending 0/1 subset DP avoids reusing a number.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n * target); Space O(n * target). Memoization stores index and remaining target.

problems.name: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
problems.question: Given an integer matrix, return the length of the longest path where each next cell is strictly larger and movement is allowed in four directions.

examples.explanation: The single cell is the path.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn log(mn)); Space O(mn). Sort cells by value and relax from smaller cells to larger neighbors.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). DFS memoization computes the best path from each cell once.

problems.name: Maximal Square
problems.question: Given a binary matrix of characters, return the area of the largest square containing only 1s.
problems.constraints: 1 <= rows, cols <= 300; matrix[i][j] is 0 or 1 as a character.

examples.explanation: The largest square has side length 2.
Each single 1 forms a square of area 1.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(rows * cols); Space O(cols). Rolling DP stores square side lengths for the current row.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(rows * cols); Space O(rows * cols). Memoized recursion computes each starting cell once.
